name: Andoque
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 10 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Landaburu, Jon. 2000. La lengua andoque. In María Stella González de Pérez & María Luisa Rodríguez de Montes (eds.), Lenguas indígenas de Colombia: una visión descriptiva, 275-288. Santafé de Bogotá: Instituto Caro y Cuervo.
catalog_locator: §10.1 Fonología: §10.1.1 'La sílaba', p. 276 and §10.1.5 'El tono', pp. 277-278; image scan without read directly.
catalog_quote: 10.1.1 La sílaba. La lengua andoque es tonal. La identificación de cada signo mínimo o morfema depende de la interpretación de su perfil melódico en una sucesión discreta de alturas musicales cuyo paradigma consta de dos posiciones. El ámbito de segmentos fónicos sucesivos dentro del cual se da una unidad discreta de altura musical es la sílaba. La sílaba andoque es de tipo: ± Consonante + Vocal [...] 10.1.5. El tono. Forma parte de la identidad del significante de un morfema andoque, no sólo la determinación de sus fonemas sucesivos, sino también la determinación de sus tonemas sucesivos. El tonema es la altura melódica fundamental contrastiva de una sílaba. No hay sino dos alturas fundamentales: una baja, una alta. Así como los fonemas pueden variar en su realización en la cadena hablada en función de los fonemas vecinos, los tonemas se pueden realizar de distinta manera según los tonemas vecinos. Llamamos tono la realización de un tonema. En la cadena hablada se dan tonos bajos, medios y altos. El tono medio es realización de un tonema bajo cuando éste se encuentra entre tonema alto y tonema bajo (regla 1) o entre tonema bajo y pausa (regla 2). [...] En la lengua, la tonalidad no diferencia muchos signos. Algunos radicales léxicos se oponen por el tono [...] El tonema bajo es mucho más frecuente que el alto. Hay índices de que la articulación de un tono alto tiende a alargar la vocal afectada.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.translation: 10.1.1 The syllable. The Andoque language is tonal. The identification of each minimal sign or morpheme depends on interpreting its melodic profile as a discrete succession of musical pitches whose paradigm has two positions. The span of successive segments within which one discrete pitch unit occurs is the syllable. The Andoque syllable is of the type (C)V [...] 10.1.5 Tone. [...] The toneme is the contrastive fundamental melodic height of a syllable. There are only two fundamental heights: a low one and a high one.
new_statements.citation: Landaburu, Jon. 2000. La lengua andoque. In M. S. González de Pérez & M. L. Rodríguez de Montes (eds.), Lenguas indígenas de Colombia: una visión descriptiva, 275-288. Santafé de Bogotá: Instituto Caro y Cuervo.
new_statements.locator: §10.1.1 'La sílaba', p. 276, and §10.1.5 'El tono', p. 277 (PDF pages 3 and 4 of the scan; scanned in, verified against the page scan)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (15-page scan scan, 800x1146 px JPEGs at 250 ppi, no text) plus its scanned. I extracted the embedded page scan (pdfimages) for PDF pages 3-5 (= printed pp. 276-278), upscaled the relevant crops and read them directly. (1) p. 276, under '10.1 FONOLOGIA': '10.1 1 La silaba. La lengua andoque es tonal. La identificacion de cada signo minimo o morfema depende de la interpretacion de su perfil melodico en una sucesion discreta de alturas musicales cuyo paradigma consta de dos posiciones. El ambito de segmentos fonicos sucesivos dentro del cual se da una unidad discreta de altura musical es la silaba. La silaba andoque es de tipo: +- Consonante + Vocal' -- matches the report's quot…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Andoque is a two-register tone language (H vs L toneme on every (C)V syllable, with contextual mid/low realizations and pre-pausal adjustments); the author's phonology (2000 §10.1, likewise 1976/1977) describes tone, vowel interruption (glottal) and length-under-H, but gives no word-stress/accent rule and never mentions 'acento' for Andoque.
new_statements.exceptions: No stress discussed. Related prosodic remarks: high tone tends to lengthen its vowel (2000: 278); tone-realization rules 1-6 incl. L -> mid before pause and H -> L after H before pause (2000: 277; 1977 'Guide de lecture' rules 1-3); Witte 1977: 288 notes that in the SIL orthography high tone is written 'only on syllables other than the penultimate' (an orthographic convention, possibly hinting at predictable penult pitch, but not stated as stress).
new_statements.domain_note: Tone-bearing unit = syllable; tone realization rules refer to pause (phrase edge). Landaburu 2004-05 (Amerindia 29/30: 13) classes Andoque with 'lenguas tonales de dos o tres registros', explicitly not with the 'acento-tonales' languages whose register contrast is limited to a prominent syllable.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the Andoque of the río Aduche community below Araracuara (Amazonas, Colombia), glottocode ando1256 / ISO ano; Landaburu 2000: 275 notes the Aduche community's speech follows the norm of the Gavilanes lineage and that former lineage dialects have levelled. Names: Andoque, Andoke; autonym pʌʌsíʌhʌ 'gente del hacha'. Witte's SIL data (1970-75, José and César Andoke) are from the same community.

tone_statements.citation: Hyman, Larry M. & William R. Leben. 2017. Word prosody II: Tone systems. UC Berkeley Phonetics and Phonology Lab Annual Report 13: 178-209. doi:10.5070/P7131040752. [Published version: Hyman, Larry M. & William R. Leben. 2020. Tone systems. In Carlos Gussenhoven & Aoju Chen (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of Language Prosody, 44-65. Oxford: Oxford University Press. doi:10.1093/oxfordhb/9780198832232.013.6]
tone_statements.quote: At one end of the density scale are languages where all tonal contrasts are fully specified and realized in all positions. Assuming that the syllable is the TBU, a /H, L/ system would thus predict two possible contrasts on monosyllabic words, four contrasts on disyllabic words, eight contrasts on trisyllabic words, and so forth, as in Andoke [Isolate; Colombia] (Landaburu 1979:48). … there are quite a number of cases where pitch levels are interpolated such that /H-L-L/ is realized H-M-L, as in Andoke [Isolate; Colombia] (Landaburu 1979:49).
tone_statements.locator: Sec. 2.5 Distributional constraints, p.187; and sec. 3.1 Vertical assimilation, p.189
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones, H and L, contrasting freely on every syllable (2, 4, 8 patterns on 1-, 2-, 3-syllable words); /H-L-L/ surfaces as H-M-L by interpolation. Stated second-hand from Landaburu 1979.

sources.note: §10.1 Fonología (pp. 276-278): 'La lengua andoque es tonal'; syllable (C)V is the domain of one of two tonemes (alto/bajo); six contextual tone-realization rules (mid tone between H and L or before pause, H lowered after H, etc.); high tone tends to lengthen its vowel; low toneme far more frequent. No mention anywhere of 'acento' / stress / intensity — the sketch is silent on word stress.

sources.note: Areal overview p. 13: lists andoque among 'lenguas tonales de dos o tres registros' (with Tucano, Bora, Makú-Puinave, ticuna), contrasted with 'lenguas acento-tonales' (piapoco, curripaco, yucuna, barasana) that keep register oppositions only on the prominent syllable. No word-stress rule for Andoque.
